contract: ScriptSpec computes a fresh full batch through original source aggregation and parser helpers. Exact compares actual extracted MC labels and normalized FF substrings; Numeric compares source-rounded finite numbers with zero tolerance. Model FF fractional scores retain the source parser and unit scale. Source prompts, SDK settings, ordered api_parallel_num concurrency, split rounding and weighted category aggregation remain.

source_oracles.rule_MC_profiles: Original complete source evaluator fails with missing number_samples. Runner wraps only the untouched per-split rule-MC result to add independently counted metadata; contract-census.json independently recomputes weighted aggregates from source per-split judgments.

corrections: Missing interpretations no longer receive random labels/fractional credit: source fixture aggregate 0.8 becomes 0. Empty model responses and stale positive cache fixtures each change 1 to 0.
Malformed judge transport/rating aborts the whole batch, retaining SDK retries but bypassing source outer 99 retries and random fallbacks.
Reject empty/nonfinite normalized references, malformed targets and reserved aggregate categories. Child InvalidTask remains invalid_task rather than infra_error.
Add missing rule-MC count metadata and map hard-benchmark generator split names to the scorer expected filenames. Fresh scoring does not trust cached judge or score files.
limitations: Fixture-only actual evaluate_responses; no archived replay or live judge inference. No matching tracker/local named traces.
PYTHONHASHSEED=0 preserves source set-list ordering in returned rule-parser observations; no cross-hash-seed ordering equivalence claim.
The internal extract_base_model_response registry option is not exposed by the benchmark constructor and is rejected if manually enabled.
Fresh scoring uses isolated temporary files and returns original result/sample shapes; existing source cache files are not trusted or replaced.
Outer Script batch deadline is 1900 seconds; malformed transport aborts without positive partial aggregates.
